newsitem.title: USA: Hearing set on Coastal Pete drilling permit.
newsitem.headline: Hearing set on Coastal Pete drilling permit.

text.p: Coastal Petroleum Co said Friday an administrative law judge has scheduled a public hearing to begin on September 29, in Tallahassee, to determine whether an offshore drilling permit should be issued to Coastal, and, if so, what conditions should be applicable.

The judge has reserved 3-1/2 to four weeks for the hearing, and has suggested that the local portion could be held in Apalachicola, the company said. It is a majority-held subsidiary of Coastal Caribbean Oils & Minerals Ltd.
Coastal, which has an 800,000-acre offshore lease-hold along Florida's Gulf Coast, has been seeking an offshore drilling permit for the past five years.
The company noted the courts have held the state has no legal basis for denying Coastal a permit but also have required that an additional administrative hearing be held.
